---
name: make-reel
description: Run the reel pipeline for one source link (an arXiv paper, or an engineering article for a system-design reel): direct, check the script on a cold viewer, produce, validate, critique, then publish according to policy. Use when the user supplies a link and wants a video made.
---
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-agents.mjs from .claude/agents. Do not edit. -->

Argument: an arXiv URL, a benchmark URL, or an engineering article URL. Optionally a format (`paper` or `system-design`).

Formats live in `paper-reels/formats/` (`explain.md` for every format, then `paper.md` and `system-design.md`). An arXiv link is `paper`. An engineering blog post or design write-up is `system-design`. If you cannot tell, ask the human before step 1.

1. Spawn `reel-director` with the URL and the format. It writes `treatment.md`. Read the chosen hook; if it is a topic label rather than a claim or question, or it uses a term a newcomer does not know, send it back once.
2. **Cold viewer, on the treatment.** Copy the `Script` block of the treatment (the spoken lines, `l01: ...`) and spawn `cold-viewer` with only those lines in the prompt: no file paths, no topic summary, no URL. Compare its say-back with the treatment's one idea. On FAIL, or when the say-back misses the idea, send its lost points and its term table to `reel-director` and check again. Stop after three rounds and report what is still unclear.
3. Spawn `reel-producer` with the URL, the treatment path and the instruction "stop at the script checkpoint". It registers the item, writes the wiki records, `storyboard.json`, `facts.json` and `evidence.json`, runs `ste.mjs` to 0 hard findings, and stops before the scenes and any voice.
4. **Cold viewer, on the storyboard.** The producer may have changed words. Extract the spoken lines (`node -e` over `storyboard.json`, `id: text` per line) and run step 2 again on them. On FAIL, send the lost points to the same producer (SendMessage) and check again, at most three rounds. On PASS, tell the same producer to continue from voice through registration, then wait for its report.
5. Spawn `reel-validator` for the item id. It runs `bin/validate.mjs` (technical, length, size and engagement gates), checks claims against the source and records the review. On FAIL, send the failures to `reel-producer` and validate again. Stop after three rounds and report what is still failing.
6. On PASS, spawn `retention-critic`. On FAIL, send its top fixes to `reel-producer` (at most two rounds), then re-validate.
7. Publishing is decided by policy, not by this skill:
   - `settings.autopublish` is off (default): show the human the verdict, scores, decoded-frame sheet, thumbnail, post text and the last cold-viewer say-back, and ask for approval. On an explicit yes in chat, record it yourself: `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs approve <id> --platforms youtube,instagram --quote "<the human's exact words>"`. Then spawn `reel-publisher`; it checks that record, because it cannot see the chat. Never run `approve` without the human's yes for these files. If the files change after the yes, show them again and ask again: the record goes stale.
   - `settings.autopublish` is on: run `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs autopublish <id>`; it posts only if every gate holds and otherwise parks the item as `needs_review` and notifies.
8. **Thread (paper only).** Once the Instagram reel of a `paper` episode is live (the reel-publisher confirmed its URL), invoke the `make-thread` skill with the paper link and the Instagram reel URL, without being asked. It drafts and checks a Threads thread and asks the human for a yes before posting (unless `settings.autopublish` is on). If the reel is not live yet, because the human has not approved posting, do not run it; say that the thread will follow after posting. A failed thread never undoes the reel. For a `system-design` episode, skip this step and say so: threads are for papers until the human decides otherwise.
9. Report the URLs (reel and thread), or what is waiting on the human.

Never skip validation or the cold-viewer check. Never let the producer judge its own output. Never run two renders of one episode at once. A `system-design` run is long (voice for 40 to 60 lines, a render of about 6 minutes): run every step in the foreground and expect it to take longer than a paper.
